head: dd2df70
summary: Retained Stage-4 HALT, not successful convergence. Fresh full direct replay completes 12 scenarios/1769 steps and exactly reproduces all 3870 ordered raw failures in the latest conductor, confirming the reset/profile/auth repair. Official groups: framework 17/19, reads 406/414, claims 279/316, drafts 225/323, AI 26/27; only reads and AI meet thresholds, and framework exceeds the waiver cap. The official board has 2187 remaining fields after 573 registered and 1110 tolerated fields. Historical local diagnostics are not official gate claims. Error-wording scoring explains 12 additional claims, 62 drafts and one AI failed case; durable-preview numbers and framework ownership/cap still block honest convergence. Strict build, format, 978 fast tests and ten Python regressions pass again. No new runtime change or push; previous 141 distinct heavy passing cases remain applicable. Head pins the verified branch before this documentation-only confirmation.

deviations.what: Stopped with a committed HALT instead of claiming all replay thresholds.
deviations.why: Stage 4 explicitly requires stopping when honest convergence cannot be claimed; framework artifact/ownership/cap conflicts and durable-preview numeric differences remain.

deviations.what: Used improvements/integrate-W2.json rather than adding a duplicate converge.json.
deviations.why: The fixed task rules and finish instructions require the session-named register; duplicate entries would misrepresent waiver ownership.

deviations.what: Reported exact local policy diagnostics, not the helper's obsolete green labels or an external conductor result.
deviations.why: The raw semantic replay remains unchanged. Exact method/template grouping, documented error-text tolerances, numeric rejection and waiver shares are explicit and tested.

deviations.what: Verified heavy cases through the complete 141-case run plus targeted repairs.
deviations.why: The initial run passed 137 and failed four merged fixtures. Both P2 repairs passed in the four-case rerun; the final 980-case fast-plus-two-heavy run passed the remaining two. Every original heavy case has a passing result; no skip or assertion suppression.

deviations.what: Distinguished 1769 recorded steps from 1765 HTTP exchanges and four controls.
deviations.why: The supplied group denominators count HTTP exchanges, while the task's earlier summary includes scenario controls in its exchange label.

deviations.what: Repaired the actual external replay entry point instead of relying on the auxiliary runner's separate scenario preparation.
deviations.why: The resumed conductor left authentication disabled and reset P2 scenarios to P1. Declared profile/auth preparation now runs through existing controls before recorded requests. Direct one-host replay reproduces independently prepared evidence; no comparison, recording or threshold changes.

deviations.what: Use the latest actual conductor board for gate claims, keeping the historical local diagnostic separate.
deviations.why: The conductor reproduces identical raw failures but scores scalar error wording and framework HTML differently. Its claims threshold is not met; the earlier local claims pass is not an official pass.

findings: Local diagnostic framework: 5 failed cases and 12 fields. Three native documentation HTML matches are rejected by its numeric prohibition. Six accepted waivers already exceed 25%.
Two g1_rest recordings expect 404 for docs/OpenAPI on a server different from the ordinary API; exact operation grouping still assigns them to framework.

Local diagnostic drafts: 36 failed cases and 239 fields. Twenty-eight cases reflect durable latest-manifest/default-program semantics; seven involve identity/base-year durability and one a wrong-method result.
Reads: 8 failed cases and 148 fields. Six concern unavailable-client or bounded-limit statuses; two involve later run identity and exact monetary-string scale.
Local diagnostic claims: 25 failed cases and 114 fields. Sixteen identity cases, three attribution-only, four status envelopes, one zero-year filter and one timestamp remain.
Python's independently unconfigured footprint reader silently returns empty state lists despite staged payroll; the configured source now reports actual states.
Python's unconfigured portal demonstration can answer an unrelated question; the offline merged host reads authorized canonical facts instead.
Stored deterministic IDs do not describe the ready-boundary UUID source state: four startup OpenTelemetry allocations are real and must be exported, not replaced with dummy draws.
Heavy fixture failures exposed stale draft-list authorization, duplicate test creation, omitted operational-table population and the intentionally retained zeroed write-sequence row.
Native DECIMAL4 formatting differs from some recorded money strings. Equal arithmetic value does not establish money-string scale equivalence.
The final replay is execution-complete, not semantically passing. The mock gateway remains deferred; sealed and unassigned buckets are not hidden.

The resumed conductor's additional failures were a real external setup defect: reset-url sent an empty body and applied no scenario auth. Raw p1_auth/P2-read/P2-batch failures dropped from 1029/888/498 to 182/148/215 after correcting that path.

Actual one-host external replay now has 3870 raw failing fields versus the earlier resumed conductor raw report's 5740. The newest conductor run reproduces every ordered failure exactly and has 2187 fields after its own policy processing.

Latest official failed cases/fields: framework 2/9, reads 8/148, claims 37/126, drafts 98/302 and AI 1/1. Earlier cluster counts above are explicitly local diagnostic measurements, not official gate counts.

Twelve additional official claims cases, 62 drafts cases and one AI case fail only on scalar error wording permitted by Tier C but not removed by the official scorer. No comparison, threshold or product wording was changed to conceal that discrepancy.
open_questions: Which server should own the g1_rest docs/OpenAPI exchanges in the merged replay?
How should framework-generated HTML and the framework waiver-cap conflict be resolved without reproducing framework artifacts?
What are the intended latest-manifest/default-program preview semantics when durable run state exists?
Which exact real persistence allocation is the first remaining post-assessment UUID divergence?

needs_human.item: Resolve framework server ownership, artifact policy and waiver-cap conflict.
needs_human.why: The official board is 17/19 with 9/19 waived (47.4%), failing both threshold and cap. The local numeric guard additionally rejects three HTML matches, yielding 14/19. Neither result passes.

needs_human.item: Reconcile durable latest-run storage and default-program preview semantics.
needs_human.why: Twenty-eight draft cases differ because real manifests replace recorded none_yet/never_run state and null program plans. Counts and identifiers cannot be waived or fabricated.

needs_human.item: Trace and reconcile remaining genuine ID allocations without removing audit durability.
needs_human.why: Early IDs match after source/assessment repairs, but later finding-audit, lookup and related allocations still diverge. The exact first later boundary is not fully established.

needs_human.item: Choose the contractual money-string scale for native DECIMAL4 writes.
needs_human.why: Strings such as 3500.0 and 3500.0000 remain different; changing to floating point or applying a numeric waiver is prohibited.

needs_human.item: Decide native storage bounds versus valid long-text request acceptance.
needs_human.why: Claim/engagement program_code and rules verified_by long values produce 500 where Python accepted them. A deliberate schema or validation contract is needed, not silent valid-value loss.

needs_human.item: Review safe unavailable-client and enormous-limit behavior for six remaining reads.
needs_human.why: Nonpositive selections must not trigger unsafe cross-client CSV fallback, and extreme limits must remain bounded. Recorded successful envelopes differ.

needs_human.item: Schedule ordinary remaining feature defects rather than treating them as improvements.
needs_human.why: Anonymous/system attribution, degraded unavailable-portfolio envelope, zero-tax-year filtering, history timestamp precision and one wrong-method outcome remain implementation backlog.

needs_human.item: Resolve seven remaining draft identity/base-year durability cases.
needs_human.why: These are real durable/identity differences separate from preview counts and cannot be hidden behind the latest-run improvement.

needs_human.item: Approve a future figure-affecting correction for M01 ingestion overrides.
needs_human.why: Ingestion still overrides year-resolved wage basis, measuring dates and pay codes, contrary to ADR-005. Explicit policy requires preserving the ported result until owner approval.

needs_human.item: Approve any future change to first-program credit pricing in a multi-program state.
needs_human.why: Credit math intentionally retains Python's first-program pricing; adding a refusal or changing pricing here would alter figures outside approval.

needs_human.item: Accept the SQL source-fingerprint limitation or choose a stronger version source.
needs_human.why: Per-account row count plus maximum modified date is an observation recorded with runs, not an immutable Delta snapshot.

needs_human.item: Align official scalar error-wording scoring with the existing Tier-C policy without changing values, shapes or thresholds.
needs_human.why: The official board retains 12 claims, 62 drafts and one AI wording-only failed case that the local diagnostic tolerates. Resolving this measurement mismatch still leaves the independently documented framework and durable-preview blockers.
